item.title: After handcuff footage, ECB takes big call on Carse before Pakistan 2nd Test
item.description: England drop Brydon Carse from the second Test against Pakistan after footage shows the fast bowler in handcuffs outside a Derby nightclub. The Cricket Regulator is investigating the incident. Carse was reportedly released without charge after celebrating Durham’s County Championship win. The episode adds to recent disciplinary concerns involving England players following other nightclub-related incidents.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan’s $125 million school to shut after 10 years
item.description: After a decade of service, The Primary School, a free private institution, has officially closed its doors. This decision follows the conclusion of financial backing from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative and the school's inability to meet state academic standards. As a result, approximately 540 students are set to transfer to the Ravenswood City Elementary School District, with the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative facilitating their transition and savings.

item.title: Mamdani’s team sends memo to ‘upset’ New Yorkers over million-dollar home tax
item.description: In a recent development, New York City's Finance Commissioner delivered a memo about the pied-à-terre tax that he could not present in person due to ongoing litigation. The memo specifies that the supplemental roll does not automatically create tax liabilities for property owners. To evade the surcharge, homeowners are encouraged to provide evidence of their primary residency. Notably, the deadline for lodging appeals has been broadened until September 18, 2026.

item.description: The Donald Trump administration said on Monday that the new US sanctions are intended to shut off every potential source of revenue for Iran, while warning other countries that continuing their economic ties with Tehran could expose them to retaliation.

item.title: Scottish medallist goes back to McDonald's job days after Commonwealth Games
item.description: Scottish judoka Summer Shaw made headlines by winning a bronze medal at the Commonwealth Games, only to head back to her part-time McDonald's job to make ends meet for her sporting endeavors. Her engaging TikTok video on the matter caught widespread interest, highlighting her need for further financial support. Eager for sponsorship, she dreams of fully committing to her judo career.

item.title: Perplexity, which wanted to buy Chrome, in talks with Nvidia for money
item.description: Perplexity, the AI search startup led by Aravind Srinivas that once made an unsolicited $34.5 billion bid for Google's Chrome browser, is now in talks with Nvidia for funding. The Information reports the round would value Perplexity above $30 billion, up more than 50 percent from its last valuation, as annualised revenue climbs past $750 million on the back of its Perplexity Computer agent.

item.title: McGregor reacts to Stone Cold meme with four words after UFC 329 exit
item.description: Conor McGregor joked that a Stone Cold Steve Austin and Vince McMahon meme matched his August. The reaction came after his UFC 329 injury and recovery. Meanwhile, Khabib Nurmagomedov described McGregor as his toughest mental challenge at that stage of his career, while making clear that Justin Gaethje later presented a harder overall fight for him inside the Octagon there.

item.title: Did Simon Nemec request a trade from Devils before Flames move?
item.description: Before becoming a member of the Calgary Flames, Simon Nemec has clarified that he did not ask for a trade from the New Jersey Devils. 22-year-old defenseman said the change of management in New Jersey and his fit in the organization were factors in the move. Nemec has since seized the opportunity in Calgary, signing to a five-year deal and expecting to play a larger role on the blue line.

item.title: Who is Avery Styles? Meet AJ Styles' son making his wrestling debut
item.description: Avery Styles, son of wrestling legend AJ Styles, has begun his professional wrestling career. He made his debut in June 2026 and quickly gained significant attention. Styles then signed a contract with TNA, a major wrestling promotion. This signing occurred after his appearance at the Lockdown event. Avery Styles is now forging his own path in the wrestling world.

item.title: Surprise protests, GenZ outreach: Rahul Gandhi's new playbook after CJP's success
item.description: Rahul Gandhi’s political style has taken a more combative turn, with the Congress leader increasingly combining Gen Z outreach, parliamentary interventions and surprise street protests. From Bharat Jodo and Chhatron Ki Goonj to student protests and dharnas, the story looks at how Rahul is trying to stay with issues longer, while also navigating criticism.

item.title: The Oval Obese: Trump's junk food habit crashes into MAHA crusade
item.description: President Trump's administration champions the importance of healthy eating and providing nutritious options to Americans. However, his fondness for fast food and sugary beverages presents a notable contradiction. This discrepancy weakens the central theme of the 'Make America Healthy Again' initiative. Health professionals emphasize that the president's weight warrants greater concern than his wardrobe, creating a dilemma for the administration in promoting healthy lifestyle choices effectively.
item.dc:creator: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA

item.title: Pant breaks another record in Colombo, surpasses Gilchrist in six-hitting feat
item.description: In a phenomenal display of skill, Rishabh Pant has outshone Adam Gilchrist's Test six record, achieving an impressive 102 sixes over just 52 matches, positioning him third globally. Additionally, he has set a new benchmark as India's highest run-scorer among wicketkeepers in away Tests, surpassing MS Dhoni's previous record. Furthermore, Pant leads India in the World Test Championship run-scorer tally.

item.title: Costa Rica spread 12,000 tonnes of orange waste; forest biomass later rose 176%
item.description: In 1998, about 12,000 metric tonnes of orange peels and pulp were spread over a degraded pasture in Costa Rica as part of an unusual forest restoration experiment. Sixteen years later, researchers found that the site had developed into a dense forest, with richer soil, greater tree diversity and a 176% increase in aboveground biomass.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Himanshi Khurana claims she has proof in Asim Riaz ‘conversion’ row
item.description: Himanshi Khurana has hit back at Asim Riaz's outright rejection of her claims, expressing her willingness to present evidence such as CCTV footage and audio recordings. She also brought to light the violence she endured during their relationship, underlining the importance of keeping her discussions respectful despite their personal nature. Khurana reiterated her right to share her experiences and lessons learned openly.
item.dc:creator: etimes.in

item.title: Nagpur chlorine leak horror: 56 hospitalised, 8 fighting for life in ICU
item.description: A chlorine gas leak at a Nagpur water treatment plant sent 56 residents to hospital. Eight patients remain in the ICU while 11 have been discharged. Emergency responders submerged the faulty chlorine tank to contain the dangerous gas. Health teams are conducting door-to-door checks for delayed symptoms. An inquiry is underway to determine the exact cause of the leakage.

item.title: US unleashes ‘Malice’: F-35C gets a 463-km air-to-air strike reach
item.description: The US Navy has introduced the AIM-424 missile, specifically engineered for the F-35C fighter jet. With a remarkable range exceeding 463 kilometers for air-to-air combat, this advanced missile maintains the aircraft's stealth attributes by allowing for internal carriage. The AIM-424 significantly boosts the F-35C's operational capabilities, while adversaries like Russia and China are rapidly advancing their own long-range missile programs.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Allahabad HC rejects Atiq Ahmed's eldest son Mohammad Umar's bail plea
item.description: The Allahabad High Court denied bail to Mohammad Umar, the eldest son of Atiq Ahmed, who is under serious allegations of extortion and threats stemming from a case filed in the previous year. Presently, he remains incarcerated in Lucknow jail. Meanwhile, his sibling Ali has been granted temporary parole for a burial, as the Atiq Ahmed family grapples with devastating losses since 2023.

item.title: India's 2026 Hockey WC semi-final race ends with 3-5 loss to Argentina
item.description: India’s men’s hockey team exit the 2026 World Cup semi-final race after losing 3-5 to Argentina. Two early goals put India on the back foot, while poor passing and missed penalty corners hurt their comeback hopes. Sukhjeet scores twice and Hardik adds a penalty stroke, but Argentina’s five-goal haul seals victory. India now play for seventh or eighth place.

item.title: From property registration to parking: What Karnataka’s 8 new Bills mean for you
item.description: Karnataka has passed eight new Bills that significantly influence property registration and land management in the state. These regulations will implement remote e-registration and bolster digital frameworks for property dealings. Unapproved rural properties must now comply with town planning guidelines. Additionally, park land can be designated for public utilities under strict oversight, while other Bills focus on refining commercial regulations and enhancing Bengaluru's transport system.

item.title: Infosys pays average 70% bonus for first quarter; staff await clarity on salary hikes
item.description: Infosys reported a 12% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 7,769 crore for the April-June quarter last month, even as it reduced its revenue growth guidance for the full year.

item.title: The unseen challenge behind every BWF World C'ships match schedule
item.description: The recently concluded BWF World Championships in New Delhi highlighted the complex task of scheduling elite badminton, as injuries, television demands and player recovery constantly reshaped the order of play. While Gayatri Gopichand and Treesa Jolly were rushed to court in an eventual win, France's Toma Junior Popov questioned uneven recovery time, exposing the delicate balance tournament referees must strike.

item.title: Kangana hits back at critics: BJP MP slams Sonu, Taapsee, Rakhi; calls Ramdev ‘failed’
item.description: Kangana Ranaut hit back at critics including Rakhi Sawant, Taapsee Pannu, Ashutosh Rana, Sonu Sood and Baba Ramdev, calling them "failed, stupid, and disgusting" for their remarks about her. She accused them of seeking media attention through abuse, said "enough is enough," and slammed Baba Ramdev for allegedly making derogatory comments about women while invoking "Sanatan Dharm."

item.description: The aunt of a deceased teenager has released an emotional video pleading for an end to unverified claims. She stated that false narratives about the family's tragedy are circulating widely on social media. The family is already struggling with immense grief and distress from the recent deaths. She appealed to social media users to consider the family left behind before posting.
